newsitem.title: USA: Fla. sees $100 mln damage to vegetables from cold.
newsitem.headline: Fla. sees $100 mln damage to vegetables from cold.

text.p: The weekend cold snap caused at least $100 million damage to Florida's vegetable crop, and the tally is rising, a state agriculture official said Tuesday.

"We're looking at $100 million and climbing. We still have people in the field doing surveys that are coming into us bit by bit," said Bob Blankenship, a spokesman for the state agriculture department. "This is some early indication that we're looking at (damage of) $100 million-plus."
Heavy losses were reported by some state farmers to their beans, squash, peppers and tomatoes, he said.

Temperatures early Sunday fell into the 20s in Miami's Dade County, surprising growers who had expected less-severe conditions. Several growers said they had depended upon the National Weather Service forecast that called for overnight lows around 40 degrees, and did not use water spraying equipment to coat the vegetables for insulation and protection.

Prices for winter vegetables were already rising quickly, according to Florida farmers. Green beans that survived the cold snap commanded $22 a bushel at a Dade County packing house Monday, up from $12 last week.

Dade County Farm Bureau estimated countywide losses of about 80 percent in squash and beans, more than 60 percent in corn and 50 percent in tomatoes. Florida growers cut back on tomato crops two years ago because of competition from Mexican imports.
Florida's east coast was largely spared, but fields of vegetables and fruit were damaged along the state's west coast as far south as Dade County, Blankenship said.
"The east coast seemed to escape and there will be produce coming out of there, but we've had as high as 70 or 80 percent losses in tomatoes over in the Immokalee area," he said.

State officials were still assessing the damage to Florida's citrus crop. Blankenship said it appeared to be limited to blooms and young orange trees but a damage estimate would not be available for several more days.
